programs.title: The Soviet Union
programs.desc: The USSR was established 100 years ago - on December 30, 1922.The filmmakers present archival materials that help answer the question of what fueled the Soviet empire throughout the 20th century.

programs.title: Border Patrol
programs.desc: The series reports on the everyday life of dedicated New Zealand customs officers, working around the clock at the country's borders.Their tasks include, among others:catching transports of drugs and other illegal items, or intercepting objects containing potentially dangerous diseases.The program's heroes also monitor people arriving in the country to prevent individuals whose presence is not welcome there from entering its territory.Viewers will find out what technology customs officers use and how trained animals support them.

programs.title: Les usines de Staline face aux armées d'Hitler
programs.desc: Historians and participants of the fighting on the Eastern Front seem to ignore the role of the Soviet economy in the victory over the Third Reich.Defeating Hitler's troops was also an economic success.

programs.title: Nazi Megastructures 6
programs.desc: Details of military solutions, tactics and technologies used by countries participating in World War II will be presented.The creators will reveal what the German anti-aircraft defense system looked like and will also talk about the Burma Death Railway.The 415 km long line was built by Japan.Its creation resulted in the death of thousands of people, mainly prisoners of war and civilians.Historians will also go on a journey around the Pacific islands, visiting places in Europe and Africa where fierce fighting took place.In the bunkers built on the territory of the Third Reich, you can still find remains of equipment and impressive fortifications.The enormous structures were intended to ensure that Hitler maintained control over the Old Continent.

programs.title: Air Crash Investigation 21
programs.desc: Reconstructions of real plane crashes.By recreating the course of events, the program's creators try to understand what led to the unfortunate events.They recreate the circumstances in which the tragedy occurred: the weather, the atmosphere on board the plane, the decisions and actions of the pilots.They also show the work of people investigating the causes of disasters and conduct a computer flight simulation.Viewers can hear various comments from specialists and testimonies of witnesses to these events.The creators of the program will prove that air accidents are often caused by human slowness and lack of imagination.Each disaster is thoroughly analyzed and the lessons learned help minimize the number of tragedies in the future.

programs.title: UFOs: Investigating the Unknown
programs.desc: New information about UFOs reinforces the need for explanations.Governments are being urged to be more transparent.The need to increase the participation of independent scientists and citizens in research is also emphasized.
